speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs (a) how many buses, goods vehicles and heavy vehicles have been involved in accidents in the last five years; (b) how many of these accidents have been caused by drivers holding work permits and S Passes; and (c) what measures are there to help bolster the efforts of our enforcement officers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Traffic Police (TP) leverages technology, for example, speeding and red-running cameras, to bolster its enforcement efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clear warning signs are erected before the TP camera enforcement zones to remind motorists to be careful and slow down.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These cameras will ensure that motorists drive at safe speeds along the entire stretch of the road.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The tachograph tracks and records vehicles' speed and other driving information.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Companies that are involved in the trial will be able to track their drivers' tachograph records and improve the drivers' driving behaviour.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Public education is also key to improving road safety.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: TP educates and engages heavy vehicle drivers on road safety and good driving practices.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: One example is the "Use Your RoadSense" movement, which was launched two years ago.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Through regular dialogues and social media platforms, the movement encourages good driving behaviour and personal responsibility amongst different road users, including heavy vehicle drivers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, what measures are in place to ensure our foreign drivers have the competencies to drive safely in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, why is there still speeding involving heavy vehicles, given that heavy vehicles have been equipped with speed limit devices?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The licence will have to be renewed every five years.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This ensures that foreign vocational drivers are subjected to the same requirements as locals before they are allowed to drive heavy vehicles here.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: However, the TP has encountered cases where heavy vehicles travelled above the speed limit.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This could have happened because the speed limiters of these vehicles were faulty or have been tampered with.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, what are the efforts to engage the workers as well as the companies, especially with the possibility that the workers may be working overtime to increase their salary before they go home.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: That is a very valid concern and we have a taskforce working with various agencies, including MOM, to see what we can do to engage the heavy vehicle drivers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The main causes of accidents involving heavy vehicles were failure to keep a proper look-out, failure to give way to traffic and failure to maintain proper control.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It may have been a result of fatigue but it may also be other factors and that is where we have to target on a holistic basis.
